source: live published KnownIssue rows plus AffiliateClick aggregates

records.title: 3.3T Oil Consumption with Smoke and Fouled Plugs
records.description: Some 3.3T owners report elevated engine-oil consumption — in one documented case roughly 2 quarts over a ~320-mile trip, accompanied by bluish exhaust smoke indicating oil burning. The consumed oil contributes to heavy intake-valve carbon (the 3.3T is direct-injected), sooty/wet spark plugs, and multi-cylinder misfire codes. Consumption is intermittent across the fleet (many cars use little to no oil), so owners should monitor levels between changes rather than assume the engine is unaffected.
records.solution: Document consumption with a dealer oil-consumption test (measured top-offs over a set mileage) while the powertrain warranty is in force. Inspect the PCV system and turbo seals for oil ingestion, replace fouled spark plugs, and clean carboned intake valves (walnut blast) if buildup is found. Check the oil level frequently between changes and use the correct spec oil; severe consumption may require dealer powertrain repair under warranty.
symptoms: Oil level dropping noticeably between changes
Bluish/grey exhaust smoke, especially on startup or under load
Low-oil warning earlier than expected
Fouled (sooty/wet) spark plugs and misfire codes
Heavy intake-valve carbon found at service

records.title: ABS Module Electrical Short Causing Engine-Bay Fire Risk (Recall 21V-161 / 007G)
records.description: An electrical short circuit can develop inside the Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) hydraulic control module. Because the module is always powered, the short can cause an engine-compartment fire whether the vehicle is parked or being driven, even with the ignition off. Genesis recalled certain 2019-2021 G70 vehicles under NHTSA campaign 21V-161 (Genesis recall 007G); owners were told to park the car outside and away from structures until repaired. This is part of the broader Hyundai/Genesis ABS-fire recall family. The remedy installs a fuse in the ABS module wiring to prevent the short from igniting a fire.
records.solution: Confirm the VIN against Recall 21V-161 (007G) and have the free remedy performed — dealers add a multi-fuse to the ABS module's power supply so a short can't start a fire. Until repaired, park outdoors away from buildings. If the ABS warning light is on or the module has already been damaged, the hydraulic electronic control unit (HECU/ABS module) is inspected and replaced as needed.
symptoms: Burning or melting-plastic smell from the engine bay
ABS / brake / traction-control warning lights illuminated
Smoke from under the hood while parked or driving
Blown fuses related to the ABS circuit

records.title: Electronic Parking Brake (EPB) Actuator Failure — Won't Release or Engage
records.description: The rear electronic parking brake actuator (rear caliper motor) can fail electrically or mechanically, leaving the EPB stuck engaged (car won't move) or refusing to set. Owners report a persistent 'Push EPB Switch' warning with a blinking EPB indicator, sometimes surfacing when the Auto Hold feature malfunctions at a stop. Because the actuator is integrated into the rear caliper assembly, dealers often replace the actuator/caliper and recalibrate rather than servicing a sub-component. Diagnostic tip from owners: press the EPB switch and listen — motor noise points to a single failed actuator, while total silence points to a switch or controller fault. This is an electromechanical actuator/control fault, distinct from any front friction-surface (rotor) issue.
records.solution: Diagnose for EPB actuator/control-module fault codes and check for a stuck Auto Hold condition. Accepted fix is replacement of the rear EPB actuator (typically as part of the rear caliper assembly) followed by system calibration/clearing via a scan tool. Some owners have reset a stuck system temporarily by pulling the relevant fuses with the engine running, but replacement is the durable fix; some cases resolved under warranty goodwill.
symptoms: 'Push EPB Switch' dashboard message
Blinking/flashing EPB warning light
Parking brake will not release, car won't move
Parking brake will not engage
Auto Hold engages brake and won't let go at a stop

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 20V569 - G70 Fuel-Pump Jet Nozzle

records.title: Front Brake Rotor Warping / Pulsation (Brembo Pad Deposit and Early Warping)
records.description: G70 owners frequently report a steering-wheel and brake-pedal pulsation that feels like warped rotors, sometimes appearing at very low mileage (reports as early as ~7,000-11,000 miles) and even all four rotors at once. On Brembo-equipped cars the cause is often uneven friction-material transfer (pad deposits) baking onto the rotor surface rather than true thickness variation — the factory ceramic-style pads don't always reach enough temperature to scrub off deposits. Some cars do show genuine early rotor distortion. Genesis has acknowledged the Brembo brake vibration concern, and the same complaint is widely documented on the platform-mate Kia Stinger.
records.solution: First try a proper bedding-in procedure (a series of firm high-speed stops) to even out and burn off pad deposits — this resolves the pulsation for many owners. If pulsation persists, measure rotor thickness variation/runout; machine or replace warped rotors and fit pads that run hotter/cleaner. Many owners upgrade to aftermarket slotted rotors and more aggressive pads. OEM front rotor for Brembo cars is 51712-J5500; DBA 4000-series slotted rotors are a common direct-fit upgrade.
symptoms: Steering-wheel shimmy or shudder when braking from highway speed
Pulsating brake pedal
Vibration felt in the seat under braking
Symptom returns a few thousand miles after rotor service

records.title: GDI Intake-Valve Carbon Buildup (Misfires, Rough Idle)
records.description: Like most gasoline direct-injection engines without supplemental port injection, the G70's 2.0T and 3.3T accumulate carbon on the backs of the intake valves over time because no fuel washes them. Owners report heavy valve coking by ~24,000 miles in some cases, especially when combined with oil consumption. The deposits disrupt airflow and seating, causing rough idle, hesitation, cold-start stumble, and cylinder misfire codes. Removing the intake to walnut-blast the valves is the definitive fix.
records.solution: Definitive repair is mechanical intake-valve cleaning (walnut-blasting / media blasting) after removing the intake manifold — typically due around 40,000-80,000 miles depending on driving and oil use. Address any contributing oil consumption (PCV/valve guides) at the same time. A quality top-tier fuel, regular oil changes, and an occasional Italian tune-up slow accumulation; catch-can installation reduces future buildup. Replace fouled spark plugs and clear misfire codes after cleaning.
symptoms: Rough or uneven idle, especially cold
Hesitation / stumble at low speed
Cylinder misfire codes, sometimes a check engine light
Reduced fuel economy and power
Hard / rough cold start

records.title: Headlight Condensation and Moisture Causing Lighting Failure
records.description: Moisture inside the headlamp assembly is one of the most widely reported G70 complaints across all model years. The vented housings draw in humid air, and when the internal seal or desiccant fails, water streaks, large droplets, or pooling collect in the housing. Persistent water intrusion can short the internal LED/turn-signal electronics, in some cases killing the blinker and requiring full assembly replacement. Genesis issued a TSB stating light fogging that clears within a few minutes is normal, but visible water streaks, large droplets, or pooling indicate a failed seal that warrants replacement. Note the 2019-2021 (pre-facelift) and 2022-2026 (facelift) headlights are completely different and not interchangeable.
records.solution: Light fogging that clears after running the headlights a few minutes is considered normal. If you see water droplets/streaks or pooling, document it (photos over time) and pursue a warranty assembly replacement — dealers replace the full headlamp unit, which requires removing the front bumper cover. Minor recurring condensation can sometimes be managed by replacing the internal desiccant pack. Confirm you order the correct generation: pre-facelift (2019-2021) vs facelift (2022-2026) assemblies are not interchangeable.
symptoms: Visible fog, water streaks, or droplets inside the headlight lens
Water pooling at the bottom of the housing
Turn signal / DRL or low-beam intermittently not working
Complete headlight failure after prolonged moisture

records.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure Causing Power Loss (Recall 24V-528 / 023G)
records.description: The fuel control valve inside the high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) can stick or allow excess fuel into the system, producing an air/fuel mixture that runs too rich. This causes a reduction or loss of motive power at low speeds, rough running, and check-engine warnings — increasing crash risk. Genesis recalled certain 2019-2023 G70 vehicles under NHTSA campaign 24V-528 (Genesis recall 023G); owner letters mailed September 2024. Many owners also reported the symptom (hesitation/near-stall when driving off within ~30 seconds of a cold start) before the formal recall. The remedy is an ECM software update plus inspection and replacement of the HPFP assembly as necessary, performed free of charge under the recall.
records.solution: First verify the VIN against Recall 24V-528 (023G) — the fix is free under recall. Dealers apply an updated ECM/engine-control software calibration and inspect the high-pressure fuel pump, replacing the pump assembly if it fails inspection. Out of warranty/recall, the OEM HPFP is replaced; the 3.3T uses Hyundai/Genesis pump 35320-3L000 and the 2.0T uses 35320-2CTB1. After replacement, clear codes and confirm fuel-rail pressure is within spec.
symptoms: Loss of power or hesitation accelerating from a stop or at low speed
Engine wants to stall if you drive off within ~30 seconds of starting
Rough running / engine surging
Check engine light, sometimes with a fuel-rail-pressure code
Long crank or hard start

records.title: Infotainment System Lag and Crashes
records.description: Early G70 models experience infotainment system lag, occasional crashes, and slow boot times. The system can take 15-30 seconds to fully initialize after starting the vehicle, and navigation inputs are sometimes delayed.
records.solution: Update to the latest head unit software via the Genesis Connected Services app or dealer visit. The 2022+ models received significant hardware and software improvements. A factory reset can resolve persistent lag issues.
symptoms: Slow system startup
Navigation lag when inputting destinations
Screen freezing requiring restart
Bluetooth audio stuttering

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11033711 - 2026 Navigation and Head-Unit Update

records.title: Limited-Slip Differential Chatter Noise
records.description: G70 models equipped with the mechanical limited-slip differential can produce a chattering or clunking noise during low-speed tight turns, such as parking lot maneuvers. The LSD clutch packs require specific friction modifier in the gear oil to operate smoothly.
records.solution: Drain and refill the differential with Hyundai/Genesis-specified gear oil containing the correct friction modifier additive. The differential may need a break-in period after fluid change. This noise is somewhat normal for clutch-type LSDs.
symptoms: Chattering noise during slow tight turns
Clunking from rear end in parking lots
Noise more pronounced on full steering lock

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Dead 12V Battery
records.description: G70 owners report the 12V battery going dead, sometimes overnight or after the car sits a few days, leaving the vehicle unable to start. Beyond normal battery aging, a recurring cause is parasitic draw — modules not fully going to sleep. The head unit/infotainment has been identified by owners as continuing to draw power with the car off, and other always-on modules can keep the draw above the normal sub-25 mA sleep target. The result is repeated no-starts even on cars with a healthy battery.
records.solution: Load-test the battery and check charging-system output first; replace the AGM battery if it fails. If the battery is good, measure parasitic draw with a multimeter after the modules sleep (target under ~25-50 mA) and pull fuses to isolate the offending circuit — the head unit/infotainment is a common culprit. Apply any infotainment/BMS software updates, and have the dealer check for related service campaigns. A battery maintainer helps cars that sit for long periods.
symptoms: Dead battery / no-crank after the car sits overnight or a few days
Slow engine crank, dim lights, clicking when starting
Battery repeatedly dies even after replacement
Electronics behaving oddly before a no-start

records.title: Power-Folding Mirror Failure (Clicking / Not Folding or Unfolding)
records.description: As G70s age, the power-folding side mirrors develop a clicking noise and fail to fold or unfold reliably — commonly the passenger mirror not unfolding on unlock, or a mirror that won't latch into the deployed position and drifts back from wind while driving. The usual cause is worn internal plastic fold gears in the mirror actuator, though some cases are an accidentally-toggled fold setting or a loose door-harness connector.
records.solution: Rule out the easy causes first: confirm the mirror-fold switch/setting wasn't bumped off, and reseat the door-harness connector (the rectangular plug with a black locking tab inside the door frame), which has fixed some cases. If the mirror clicks and won't move, the actuator's internal fold gears are stripped — replace the fold motor/gear set or the mirror actuator assembly. Severe cases require the full mirror assembly.
symptoms: Clicking/grinding noise when mirrors try to fold or unfold
Passenger mirror doesn't unfold on unlock
Mirror won't latch out and folds back from wind while driving
One or both mirrors stop folding entirely

records.title: Soft Clear Coat — Easy Chipping, Peeling and Swirl Marks
records.description: Owners across Genesis models, including the G70, report unusually soft paint and clear coat. The clear coat scratches and swirls very easily (even careful washing can mar it), the front end picks up many rock chips in only a few thousand miles, and some cars develop clear-coat bubbling or peeling — typically at the bumper, roof rails and panel edges — exposing the base coat. It mirrors the well-documented paint complaints on the Kia Stinger. While cosmetic, it drives meaningful owner dissatisfaction and out-of-pocket repaint/PPF costs.
records.solution: For chips and stone damage, paint protection film (PPF) on the hood, fenders and mirrors is the most common preventive fix. For swirls, use proper two-bucket wash technique and a light machine polish followed by a ceramic coating to add a sacrificial layer. Document clear-coat bubbling/peeling early and pursue it under the paint warranty — some dealers have repainted affected panels for owners showing adhesion failure.
symptoms: Numerous rock chips on the front end at low mileage
Swirl marks / fine scratches appearing from normal washing
Clear coat bubbling or peeling at bumpers, roof rails or edges
Base/flat paint showing through where clear coat lifted

records.title: Sunroof / Headliner Rattle and Creaking Noise
records.description: A rattle, creak, or crackling sound (often described like squeezing a plastic bottle) coming from the sunroof area or front headliner is a common G70 complaint, frequently emerging after only a few thousand miles. The noise is often worse in hot weather (around 80F+), over bumps and in turns, and can be traced to the sunroof glass-guide rail mount (a 'foot' that rests on a protrusion and rattles when not properly seated) or insufficient clearance between the roof sheet metal and the headliner.
records.solution: Have the dealer diagnose under warranty — fixes have ranged from repositioning/shimming the sunroof rail 'foot,' adding felt/foam or 3M tape at contact points, to ordering a replacement sunroof assembly when the rattle can't be resolved in the shop. Owners have had partial success self-treating the sunroof foot with felt tape. Confirm whether any related sunroof-noise service bulletin applies to the VIN.
symptoms: Rattle or creak from the sunroof / front headliner area
Noise worse in hot weather, over bumps, and in turns
Crackling 'plastic bottle' sound near the A-pillar / grab handle
Goes away when pressing up on the headliner

records.title: Torque Converter Internal Rivet Damage — Scratching Noise / Low-Speed Stall (Campaign T27G)
records.description: Certain 2023 G70 2.0T models built between April 14, 2022 and June 14, 2022 can suffer internal rivet damage and cracks inside the torque converter. Symptoms are a scratching/grinding noise and, in rare cases, an engine stall at idle or creep speeds, and the fault can set a torque-converter-clutch code. Genesis addressed this with Service Campaign T27G (TSB 23-01-003G), which replaces the torque converter. Importantly, on these cars a stall should be checked against this campaign before any ECM is condemned.
records.solution: Confirm the VIN and production date against Service Campaign T27G (TSB 23-01-003G). The remedy is replacement of the torque converter at no charge for affected vehicles. If you have a low-speed stall or scratching noise on a 2023 2.0T, have the dealer investigate this campaign first — do not let the ECM be replaced before the torque converter is ruled out.
symptoms: Scratching or grinding noise from the transmission area
Engine stall at idle or creep speeds (rare)
Torque-converter-clutch fault code
Shudder or roughness at very low speed

citations.title: Genesis Campaign T27G - G70 Torque Converter

records.title: 8-Speed Automatic Shift Quality Issues
records.description: The 8-speed automatic transmission in the G70 can exhibit rough or delayed shifts, particularly the 1-2 and 2-3 upshifts during cold operation. The adaptive transmission control module sometimes hunts between gears during light throttle city driving.
records.solution: Perform a transmission adaptation reset at the dealer. Update the TCM software to the latest calibration. Allow the transmission to fully warm up before spirited driving. A fluid change at 60,000 miles can improve shift quality.
symptoms: Harsh 1-2 upshift when cold
Gear hunting during city driving
Hesitation on downshift during passing

records.title: Left Turbocharger Oil Feed Line Leak (Recall 24V-191)
records.description: On 3.3T 2019-2022 G70s, the left turbocharger's oil feed pipe assembly can degrade and leak under sustained heat cycling. Oil contacting hot exhaust components creates a fire hazard. NHTSA recall 24V-191 (Genesis campaign 019G) covers free replacement with a redesigned stainless steel pipe — the same pipe Genesis fitted from the factory on 2023+ cars, which is why the recall excludes those years. Symptoms include burning-oil smell from the engine bay, oil pooling on the underbody shield, and intermittent oil pressure warnings.
records.solution: Replace the banjo bolt crush washers with new copper washers at both turbocharger oil feed connections. Inspect the oil feed lines for cracking. Torque banjo bolts to specification to prevent over-tightening.
symptoms: Burning oil smell after highway driving
Oil drips on turbo heat shields
Slight oil consumption increase
Smoke visible from engine bay after hard driving

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 24V191 - G70 Turbo Oil-Feed Pipe

records.title: Electrified G80 Software and Charging Issues
records.description: The Electrified G80 experiences occasional software-related issues including incorrect range estimates, failed DC fast charging sessions, and 12V battery management faults. The EV-specific software is still maturing compared to the ICE platform.
records.solution: Update to the latest EV software through the dealer or OTA. Reset the BMS by disconnecting the 12V battery for 30 minutes. Report failed charging sessions to Genesis Connected Services for remote diagnostics.
symptoms: Range estimate fluctuating wildly
DC fast charging stopping prematurely
12V battery warning messages
Preconditioning not activating

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 26V019 - G80 Instrument Display Software

records.title: Infotainment System Software Glitches
records.description: The G80 infotainment system experiences intermittent software glitches including screen blackouts, navigation errors, and unresponsive touch inputs. OTA updates have introduced new bugs while fixing existing ones on several occasions.
records.solution: Keep the system updated to the latest firmware. Perform a factory reset after major OTA updates. Visit the dealer for a head unit reflash if persistent issues occur. The rotary controller can be used as a backup input method.
symptoms: Screen going black momentarily
Navigation giving incorrect directions
Touch inputs not registering
System rebooting while driving

records.title: 5.0L Tau V8 GDI intake-valve carbon buildup and some oil consumption
records.description: The 5.0L Tau V8 is gasoline-direct-injection only (no port injectors to wash the valves), so intake valves accumulate carbon deposits over time, which can cause rough idle, misfire and reduced performance at higher mileage. Some 2018+ owners also report elevated oil consumption (adding oil between changes), though rates are often within Genesis's acceptable spec.
records.solution: Perform periodic walnut-blast (media) cleaning of the intake valves to remove carbon; use Top Tier 91-93 octane fuel and occasional higher-rpm driving to slow deposit formation, plus an intake-cleaning additive service. Monitor oil consumption with regular level checks between changes; document consumption for warranty if it exceeds spec.
symptoms: Rough idle
Cold-start misfire/stumble
Reduced power at higher mileage
Needing to add oil between changes
Check-engine light for misfire

records.title: 8-speed automatic harsh/jerky upshifts and low-speed lurch (solenoid TSB)
records.description: Owners report harsh, jerky 2-3, 3-4 and 4-5 upshifts, hesitation and a low-speed lurch/jerk on the 8-speed automatic. A subset of 2018 V6 cars reported the transmission slipping toward Neutral from Drive/Reverse. Hyundai/Genesis issued a TSB attributing harsh upshifts to two shift solenoids that were upgraded.
records.solution: Have the dealer apply the harsh-shift TSB (upgraded shift solenoids) and perform a transmission adaptive-value reset so the TCM relearns shift points. Verify fluid level/condition. Many owners find Sport mode's shift profile smooths hesitation as an interim workaround.
symptoms: Harsh/banging upshifts
Jerk or lurch at low speed
Shift hesitation/flare
Momentary slip toward Neutral (some 2018)
Clunk on acceleration

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10163285 - 8-Speed Harsh or Delayed Shift

records.title: Air suspension failures — leaking air struts/bags, compressor burnout and rear sag
records.description: First-generation G90s use an electronically controlled air suspension that is a recurring high-cost failure point. Owners report pinhole leaks in the air struts/bags, failed leveling (height) sensors, exploded air dryers and burnt-out compressors, producing a saggy or uneven stance, knocking noises over bumps and a harsh ride. Repeated compressor/strut failures can run into the thousands of dollars. Genesis abandoned this air-suspension design on the redesigned G90.
records.solution: Diagnose the specific failed component: replace leaking air struts/bags, the compressor (often failing after it runs continuously trying to keep up with a leak), the air dryer, or a faulty height/leveling sensor. A dealer-only suspension ECU reboot/reset can resolve a rear that sags on startup when no leak is present. Fix leaks promptly to avoid killing the compressor.
symptoms: Rear or corner sagging
Uneven ride height
Knocking/clunking over bumps
Harsh ride
Compressor runs constantly
Suspension warning message

records.title: Blank instrument cluster on startup due to LG software logic error
records.description: A software bug supplied by LG Electronics in the digital instrument cluster causes the entire IP display to go blank at startup on 2023-2025 G90s built Apr 21, 2022 - Apr 7, 2025. With no speedometer, warnings, or system status visible, the condition violates FMVSS 101. Genesis recall 027G / NHTSA campaign covers 2,345 G90 units (part of a 4,754-vehicle total with GV60).
records.solution: Recall 027G: free OTA software update pushed to the cluster, or a dealer flash if OTA fails. If your cluster is blank, do not drive — pull over, key-cycle, and contact Genesis at 844-340-9741 (reference recall 027G). Owner notification letters were mailed no later than September 15, 2025.
symptoms: blank instrument cluster at startup
no speedometer
missing warning lights
intermittent display dropout

records.title: Coolant leaks from water pump and thermostat housing
records.description: Coolant weeping/leaks are frequently reported and seen by technicians on first-gen G90s — commonly from the water pump and thermostat housing on the 3.3T, plus O-ring/gasket seepage on the 5.0. Left unaddressed, slow coolant loss risks overheating and cylinder-head damage on the Lambda/Tau V6/V8 family.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system to pinpoint the source. Replace the water pump (G90 water pump PN 25100-3F300) and/or thermostat housing with new gaskets; clean and flatten mating surfaces and torque bolts in sequence to spec to avoid a repeat leak. Refill with the correct Hyundai/Genesis long-life coolant and bleed air.
symptoms: Low coolant / needing top-offs
Sweet coolant smell
Coolant residue at front of engine
Overheating
Puddle under vehicle

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10158795 - G90 ATF-Warmer Coolant Leak

records.title: Fuel crossover pipe leaks at engine rail (under-torqued fasteners) - fire risk
records.description: On the second-generation 3.5L twin-turbo G90, the retention fasteners on the fuel crossover pipe at the fuel-rail connections were tightened during assembly with an insufficient concentration of thread/torque stabilizer (thread retainer). Over time the fasteners can gradually loosen, allowing gasoline to seep from the crossover pipe joints. Fuel leaking near hot engine components creates an engine-fire hazard. This is a manufacturing/assembly-torque defect covered by NHTSA recall 26V229 (Genesis campaign 033G). It affects 4,231 G90 units within a larger ~94,760-vehicle Genesis action (G80/GV80/GV70 also covered), part of a combined ~235,000-unit Kia-Genesis fuel-leak action. It is a fuel-delivery-rail failure distinct from the low-pressure fuel-pump impeller recall and the turbo oil-feed-pipe fire recall.
records.solution: Under recall, dealers inspect the fuel crossover pipe and its fasteners, re-tighten them to spec with the correct torque stabilizer, and replace the fuel pipe if a leak or damage is found - free of charge regardless of warranty status, with reimbursement for prior out-of-pocket repairs. NHTSA advises parking outside and away from structures until the repair is done. VINs became searchable on NHTSA.gov April 11, 2026 and owner letters were mailed June 8, 2026.
symptoms: Fuel odor around the engine bay or under the hood
Fuel stains/wet residue near the fuel rail
Risk of engine-compartment fire

records.title: Infotainment/navigation screen freezes or goes blank, requiring reboot
records.description: The DIS infotainment/navigation head unit intermittently freezes, becomes unresponsive, or displays a blank screen — including a 'Navigation Activation in Progress' message that leaves the map unavailable. It can also drop Bluetooth/connectivity. Distinct from the second-gen instrument-cluster software recall; this is the center-stack head unit on first-gen cars.
records.solution: Soft-reboot by holding the MAP and SETUP hard buttons together until the screen goes black and the Genesis logo appears (or hold power 10-15s). Apply the latest navigation/firmware update via dealer or USB. Persistent cases have been resolved by head-unit software reflash or replacement under warranty; a battery-cable disconnect can clear a stuck boot.
symptoms: Frozen/unresponsive touchscreen
Blank center display
'Navigation Activation in Progress' stuck message
Bluetooth/USB dropouts
System reboots on its own

records.title: Intermittent dashboard warning cascade with electronic parking brake lockout
records.description: Multiple 2023 G90 owners report sudden 'dashboard lit up like a Christmas tree' events: every warning light illuminates, a 'STOP ENGINE / check brake system' message appears, and the electronic parking brake refuses to release, stranding the vehicle. One documented dealer diagnosis was a shorted main sensor, but the fault is intermittent and recurred one week after repair. Separate 2023 G90 electrical complaints (dead battery, door handles not deploying) suggest a broader pattern of low-voltage / sensor faults on the new RS4 generation.
records.solution: Document every occurrence with date, mileage, and a photo of the cluster. Demand a parasitic-draw test and scan of all CAN modules. If the fault recurs after sensor replacement (commonly the body-control or yaw module), escalate to Genesis case management — multiple owners have qualified for lemon-law buyback once events exceed 30 days down or 3+ repair attempts.
symptoms: all dashboard warning lights illuminate simultaneously
STOP ENGINE / check brake system message
electronic parking brake malfunction
vehicle may be immobilized
intermittent re-occurrence after sensor replacement
associated parasitic battery drain
associated false TPMS warnings

records.title: Left turbocharger oil feed pipe cracks and leaks oil onto exhaust manifold, causing engine-compartment fire
records.description: On G90s equipped with the 3.3L twin-turbo V6, the original left-hand turbocharger oil feed pipe and hose assembly was manufactured from a material that becomes brittle after prolonged heat exposure and repeated heat/cool cycling. The pipe cracks and leaks pressurized engine oil directly onto the hot exhaust manifold, dramatically increasing the risk of an under-hood fire. This drove NHTSA Recall 24V191 (Hyundai/Genesis campaign 019G), which expanded and replaced earlier campaign 19V-538. Owners are warned it can ignite whether parked or driving.
records.solution: Under recall 019G the dealer replaces the left turbo oil feed pipe/hose with an improved, more durable (stainless-reinforced) part free of charge. OEM left oil feed pipe/hose assembly is Hyundai PN 28240-3L100 (service kit references 28240-3L122QQH); inspect for oil weeping at the turbo and manifold, and address any oil-soaked heat shielding at the same time.
symptoms: Burning oil smell
Oil smoke from engine bay
Low oil level
Oil drips/residue near left turbo and exhaust manifold
Fire warning / under-hood fire

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 24V191 - G90 Turbo Oil-Feed Pipe

records.title: Low-pressure fuel pump impeller deforms in heat, causing stalling (NHTSA Recall 24V282000)
records.description: Per NHTSA Recall 24V282000 / Genesis 022G, low-pressure fuel pump assemblies in ~1,364 G90 sedans (2022-2023 MY, built Jun 2, 2021 - Sep 14, 2022) may contain impellers that deform under high ambient/underhood temperatures, causing mechanical interference with the pump housing and shutdown. Affects both 1st-gen (3.3T Lambda / 5.0L V8) 2022 G90s and 2nd-gen (3.5T Smartstream) 2023 G90s — two distinct pump part numbers in the recall (31110-D2000 Theta-family applicator and 31110-T1050 Lambda-family applicator across the campaign).
records.solution: Recall 022G (NHTSA 24V282000): Genesis dealer inspects and replaces the low-pressure fuel pump assembly free of charge. Owner notification mailed June 18, 2024. Check VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or call Genesis at 1-855-371-9460. Do not delay — a sudden fuel pump shutdown in traffic increases crash risk.
symptoms: check engine light
engine hesitation
rough running
sudden stall while driving
no-start after heat soak

records.title: Panoramic sunroof creaking, rattling and wind noise (loose/under-torqued frame bolts)
records.description: First-generation (DH) G90 sedans with the large panoramic glass roof commonly develop creaks, rattles and squeaks from the roof/headliner area, plus wind-noise vibration over the glass. Root causes owners and dealers have found include sunroof frame/track attachment bolts that back off or were under-torqued from the factory (one documented case found 32 loose bolts), plus metal-on-metal contact in the frame. Genesis addresses the noise complaints with TSB 23-BD-014G. Note: some owners also report spontaneous panoramic-glass shattering (a known Hyundai/Kia glass-roof failure mode), but that is less well documented specifically on the G90 and coverage is often disputed absent proven breakage.
records.solution: Per TSB 23-BD-014G, install the sunroof felt/anti-noise kit (adds felt padding and lubricant to stop metal-on-metal movement) and fit modified sunroof frame bolts torqued to spec; loose factory bolts are re-torqued. In stubborn cases the roof/sunroof frame assembly is replaced. For a shattered glass panel, the sunroof glass or full assembly is replaced.
symptoms: Creaking/squeaking from the roof or headliner over bumps
Rattling or buzzing from the sunroof glass area
Excessive wind noise or vibration at highway speed
Loud bang and glass falling into cabin (spontaneous glass shatter, less common)

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10154546 - G90 Panoramic Sunroof Noise

records.title: Power trunk fails to close/latch or release, often due to lid misalignment
records.description: Owners of the power-operated trunk on the first-generation G90 report intermittent failures where the decklid will not fully close and latch when lowered, or will not release and rise when commanded (some report a stick roughly every few openings). The trunk uses a power latch (cinch) module and a power drive (raise/lower) module, either of which can fail or fall out of calibration. Owner and dealer reports indicate lid misalignment is a frequent root cause - striker, rubber stopper and trim adjustment often resolves it - and that simply replacing the latch and drive motor does not always help. Low 12V battery voltage can also cause the symptom. This is a body/closure electromechanical issue distinct from the general parasitic battery-drain complaint.
records.solution: Dealers typically start by adjusting the striker, bump stops/rubber stoppers and plastic trim to correct alignment, and check the release switch/harness and battery voltage; a full re-charge sometimes restores operation. Where the actuators are actually failed, the power latch assembly and/or power drive unit are replaced and the trunk initialization/re-learn is run. Under warranty the repair is free; out of warranty, actuator/latch parts plus labor typically run several hundred to over a thousand dollars.
symptoms: Trunk does not fully close/cinch when lowered
Trunk fails to open or release when the button/fob is pressed
Intermittent, hard-to-reproduce operation (e.g., every few tries)
Trunk-ajar warning despite the lid appearing shut

records.title: Repeated 12V battery drain / dead battery from head unit and modules drawing power when parked
records.description: Owners across model years report the 12V battery going flat after the car sits a few days. A common documented culprit is the radio/head unit continuing to draw current after shutdown, along with other parasitic draws that exceed the normal <50 mA key-off current. Leaving the key fob near the car can compound it. Frequent deep discharges shorten battery life and can leave the car unable to start.
records.solution: Measure key-off parasitic draw with a clamp/multimeter (target under ~50 mA); pull fuses to isolate the offending circuit. Where the head unit is the source, dealers have replaced it under warranty. Replace a degraded battery, keep the fob away from the vehicle when parked, and use a maintainer for cars that sit.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting a few days
Slow cranking / no-start
Repeated jump-starts
Battery drains overnight
Electronics stay awake after lock

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11008141 - G90 DIS2.0 Battery Drain

records.title: Savile Silver paint reflects corner radar, triggering phantom automatic emergency braking (Highway Drive Assist)
records.description: On G90s painted in Savile Silver, the aluminum-heavy paint formulation at the corners of the front bumper cover reflects the corner-radar signal back into the sensor. Highway Drive Assist (HDA) interprets the reflection as a vehicle cutting into the lane and applies sudden, unintended braking — reported at low speed (below ~12 mph) and when Lane Change Assist is active. Only Savile Silver cars are affected. Covered by NHTSA Recall 25V833 (483 U.S. vehicles).
records.solution: Under recall 25V833 a certified Genesis technician seals the front bumper beam so the radar signal is not transmitted through the body panel to strike the paint. Free of charge. As an interim measure owners can disable HDA/forward-collision-assist braking if experiencing phantom braking, and confirm the bumper-beam remedy has been applied.
symptoms: Sudden unintended braking
Phantom emergency braking with no obstacle
False forward-collision alerts
Braking when Lane Change Assist engaged

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 25V833 - G90 Highway Drive Assist

records.title: Seat-belt pretensioner over-pressurization can rupture and eject metal fragments
records.description: On the 2023 G90, the front driver, front passenger, and rear seat-belt pretensioners can over-pressurize when they deploy in a crash. The micro-gas-generator pretensioner pipe may rupture, causing abnormal deployment that sprays metal fragments into the cabin and risks injuring occupants. This is the same defective pyrotechnic pretensioner family behind a broader Genesis/Hyundai action; the G90-specific slice is NHTSA recall 23V210 (Genesis campaign 013G), covering roughly 575 units built April 21, 2022 through February 21, 2023. It is a restraint-system safety defect entirely separate from the electrical, fuel, and drivetrain issues catalogued elsewhere. At filing, Genesis was not aware of any real-world abnormal deployment incidents.
records.solution: Dealers install a securing cap on the seat-belt pretensioners so that, even if a pretensioner over-deploys, the assembly is contained and cannot fling metal fragments into the occupant space. The remedy is performed free of charge; owner notification letters were mailed in May 2023.
symptoms: No pre-crash symptoms - latent defect only manifests during pretensioner deployment in a collision
Potential for metal fragments/shrapnel in the cabin after belt/airbag deployment

records.title: Water intrusion into starter solenoid causes electrical short and engine-compartment fire
records.description: Water can enter the starter solenoid and cause an electrical short, which may lead to an engine-compartment fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven. Genesis instructed owners to park outside and away from structures until repaired. Covered by NHTSA Recall 24V107 (Hyundai/Genesis campaigns 018G and 254(H)); owner notification letters were mailed July 15, 2024.
records.solution: Under recall 24V107, dealers install a remedy relay kit in the engine junction box that de-energizes the starter circuit when the engine is running, preventing solenoid overheating/short — performed free of charge. No customer parts purchase required; verify the relay kit was installed if buying used.
symptoms: Burning/electrical smell
Smoke from engine bay
Blown starter fuse
No-start
Under-hood fire while parked

records.title: 12V Battery Drain When Parked
records.description: The GV60 can experience excessive 12V auxiliary battery drain when parked for extended periods. Connected services modules, security systems, and over-the-air update checks continue drawing power, depleting the small 12V battery within 5-7 days of inactivity.
records.solution: Keep the vehicle plugged in when parked for more than 3 days to allow the HV system to maintain the 12V battery. Update to the latest software that includes improved power management. A 12V battery maintainer can be used as a backup.
symptoms: Vehicle will not start after sitting several days
Key fob unable to unlock doors
Multiple warning messages after jump start
Connected services disconnecting

records.title: OTA Software Update Failures
records.description: The GV60 OTA (over-the-air) update process occasionally fails mid-installation, leaving the vehicle in a partially updated state. Failed updates can cause infotainment malfunctions, ADAS feature deactivation, or charging management errors.
records.solution: Ensure the vehicle is plugged in with a strong cellular signal during OTA updates. If an update fails, visit the dealer for a complete software reflash. Do not interrupt the update process by starting the vehicle.
symptoms: Update progress bar stuck
Infotainment not booting after update
ADAS features showing as unavailable
Charging schedule not functioning after update

records.title: Range Estimate Inconsistency
records.description: The GV60 range estimation algorithm shows significant variability, with actual range often falling 15-25% short of the displayed estimate in cold weather or at sustained highway speeds above 70 mph. The system does not adequately factor in ambient temperature and driving speed.
records.solution: Precondition the battery and cabin while plugged in before departure. Use ECO mode and limit climate control usage in cold weather for maximum range. The BMS improves range predictions after learning driving patterns over several thousand miles.
symptoms: Range dropping faster than expected
Cold weather range loss exceeding 25%
Highway range significantly less than city range

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain and Dead-Battery 'Bricking'
records.description: Owners across both the ICE and Electrified GV70 report the 12V battery going dead after the car sits for only a few days, leaving the vehicle unresponsive and unable to start ('bricked'). Genesis Roadside and dealers have told owners the car must be driven 30 minutes every 3-7 days to keep the 12V charged. Reported root causes vary: parasitic draw from electronic modules and telematics, the key fob staying in constant communication when left in the car, a weak/corrupt-cell 12V battery, loose wiring, and on Electrified models a failing ICCU not charging the 12V. The pattern is frequent enough that many owners run battery tenders.
records.solution: Have the dealer perform a parasitic-draw test and load-test the 12V battery; replace the battery if a cell is bad (often done under warranty). Keep the key fob out of the car when parked for long periods, and on cars that sit, use a battery tender or drive ~30 minutes weekly. On Electrified GV70s, confirm the ICCU recalls (025G / 24V-204 family) are completed, since ICCU failure is a major cause of repeat 12V deaths. Persistent draw with no obvious cause warrants module-by-module isolation by the dealer.
symptoms: Car dead/unresponsive after sitting a few days
No-start, no dash lights, doors won't respond
Repeated need to jump-start
Battery dies again shortly after replacement
Warning to drive the vehicle to charge the battery

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10244961 - VCU and 12-Volt Battery-Saver Update

records.title: 8-Speed Automatic Jerky Downshift Syndrome (JDS) and Throttle Response Lag (Gasoline Models)
records.description: Gasoline GV70 owners (2.5T and 3.5T) report a throttle-tip-in delay followed by an abrupt jolt, plus hard or jerky downshifts from the 8-speed automatic (Hyundai A8LR1/A8TR1), most noticeable accelerating out of a turn or in Sport mode. The community calls it 'Jerky Downshift Syndrome' (JDS); Genesis is aware and has been unable to deliver a permanent fix, performing an adaptive-transmission-value (ATV) reset that helps temporarily before the transmission relearns the behavior. The hesitation prompts drivers to press harder, causing lurching. This is a transmission/throttle calibration problem distinct from the low-pressure fuel-pump stalling issue.
records.solution: A 2023 technical bulletin covers replacing the transmission solenoids, resetting adaptive transmission values, running the oil-pressure characteristics input procedure, and TCM adaptive-value relearn. A powertrain/TCU software reflash to smooth shift and throttle mapping is done under warranty. In hardware cases, dealers have replaced the throttle body (and, for some, fuel injectors), which resolved the hesitation; a minority of intermittent cases traced to coolant leaks putting the car in limp mode were fixed by hose/radiator repair.
symptoms: Delay between pressing the accelerator and the car responding
Car jolts or lurches forward after the delay
Hard or jerky downshifts, especially in Sport mode
Hesitation/lag when accelerating out of a turn
Drivetrain feels rough or 'cheap' at low speed

records.title: Front Brake Squeal and Dust
records.description: The GV70 front brakes produce excessive brake dust and a high-pitched squeal during light braking, especially in the morning or after the vehicle has been sitting. The aggressive brake pad compound prioritizes stopping power over noise and cleanliness.
records.solution: Replace the front brake pads with a low-dust ceramic compound. Clean and lubricate the brake caliper slide pins and pad contact points. Apply brake pad shim adhesive if shims are loose or missing.
symptoms: High-pitched squeal during light braking
Excessive black brake dust on front wheels
Grinding noise after car sits overnight

records.title: A/C Not Cooling / Weak Cooling on One Side
records.description: Owners report the air conditioning not blowing cold, or cooling unevenly (commonly warm air from the driver-side vents while the passenger side is cold) on the dual-zone climate system. Reported causes include a refrigerant leak/undercharge, an electrical climate-control fault, and AC compressor problems; a dealer in one forum case attributed weak cooling to the compressor after seeing it on related Genesis models (GV80). It is a high-search comfort complaint, especially in hot climates.
records.solution: Have the dealer leak-test and verify refrigerant charge first, then check the climate-control actuators/blend doors and compressor operation. Fixes range from recharging and sealing a leak to replacing a blend-door actuator or, in confirmed cases, the AC compressor. Repairs in the warranty window should be covered; out of warranty, expect compressor replacement to be the costliest path.
symptoms: A/C not blowing cold
Driver-side vents warm while passenger side is cold (or vice versa)
Cooling fades after the system runs a while
Hissing or no cold air after a refrigerant leak
Climate system blowing ambient-temperature air

records.title: Electrified GV70 Range Inconsistency
records.description: The Electrified GV70 shows significant variation between estimated and actual driving range, particularly in cold weather. The range estimate algorithm does not adequately account for cabin heating, terrain, and highway speeds, leading to range anxiety.
records.solution: Precondition the battery while plugged in before cold weather departures. Use ECO mode for maximum range. The BMS learns driving patterns over time and range estimates improve after 2,000-3,000 miles of ownership.
symptoms: Range estimate dropping faster than miles driven
Significant range loss in cold weather
Inconsistent range between identical trips

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10238386 - Electrified GV70 Charging Update

records.title: Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist Phantom / Unwanted Automatic Emergency Braking
records.description: Gasoline and Electrified GV70 owners report the Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist (FCA/AEB) and its front radar/camera triggering false Forward Collision Warnings and applying the brakes when no real hazard is present. Commonly reported scenarios documented in owner forums: unexpected brake application at 70-80 mph when changing lanes to reach an off-ramp, braking during overtaking as the vehicle merges back into its lane (which can look like brake-checking the passed car), and false triggers on curves where the radar reads a slower vehicle in an adjacent lane as being in the driver's lane. This is an ADAS/sensor-calibration fault, distinct from the fuel-pump stall and ICCU loss-of-power issues.
records.solution: Dealers inspect and recalibrate or clean the front radar and windshield camera; a control-module software update is applied where available. When recalibration does not fully resolve it, owners reduce FCA warning sensitivity to 'late' or disable FCA in heavy traffic as a workaround. Most calibration/software work is covered under the new-vehicle warranty.
symptoms: Vehicle brakes hard for no visible obstacle
False Forward Collision Warning alerts on open highway
Unexpected braking during lane changes or while overtaking
Radar reads adjacent-lane vehicle as in-lane on curves
Alarm and dashboard warning accompanying the phantom braking event

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11016993 - Front Radar DTC C162078

records.title: Fuel Pipe-to-Rail Connection Leak Fire Risk
records.description: Fuel can leak at the pipe connection between the high-pressure fuel pipe and the fuel rail. A fuel leak in the engine bay near hot components raises the risk of an underhood fire. Genesis issued safety recall 033G (NHTSA 26V-229) in April 2026 covering roughly 26,000 GV70 from the 2022-2026 model years (part of a larger ~235,000-vehicle Kia/Genesis action). Owners may notice a fuel smell or fuel odor around the engine bay.
records.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recall 26V-229 (Genesis 033G). Dealers will inspect and tighten the fuel pipe connection, or replace the fuel pipe as necessary, free of charge. Owner letters began mailing June 8, 2026. If you smell raw fuel, stop driving and have it inspected immediately rather than waiting for the recall appointment.
symptoms: Fuel smell or raw gasoline odor around the engine bay
Visible fuel residue or wetness near the fuel rail
Fuel smell after refueling or under load

records.title: Headlight Assembly Moisture and Condensation Buildup
records.description: A frequently cited exterior/lighting complaint on the GV70 is moisture and condensation forming inside the LED headlight housings, ranging from light fogging after a car wash to visible water pooling at the bottom of the assembly. Owners report the condensation blurs the LED beam pattern, reduces nighttime illumination, and raises the risk of premature LED failure from repeated water-vapor exposure. Some owners have had assemblies replaced under warranty for recurring condensation. This is a sealing/venting issue distinct from any electrical charging or cluster fault.
records.solution: Genesis addresses it via Technical Service Bulletin (TSB 22-BD-002G, also issued as 23-BD-002G / NHTSA 10230903) rather than a recall. Technicians run the headlights (high beam) for a minimum of 30 minutes; a small clearing mist is deemed normal, but persistent water droplets, streaks, or pooling indicate a failed seal and the assembly is replaced under the new-vehicle warranty. Out of warranty, a full LED assembly replacement is expensive.
symptoms: Fog or condensation inside the headlight lens
Water pooling at the bottom of the headlamp housing
Blurred or dimmed LED beam / reduced night illumination
Condensation recurring after previous replacement
Water droplets/streaks that do not clear after running lights

records.title: ICCU Failure Causing Loss of Drive Power (Electrified GV70)
records.description: The Integrated Charging Control Unit (ICCU) manages charging of the high-voltage pack and the 12V battery that runs accessories and control modules. The ICCU (and its internal fuse) can become damaged and stop charging the 12V system. The car then enters a fail-safe mode with warning lights, audible alerts, and reduced power; if driving continues it can fully lose drive power, sometimes preceded by an audible 'pop.' Drivers typically have ~22-45 minutes to pull over, with steering and brakes still functional. Genesis covered this under recalls tied to NHTSA 24V-204, expanded/replaced by Genesis 025G (Dec 2024), part of the broad Hyundai/Kia/Genesis ICCU campaign. The failed ICCU also produces dead-12V 'bricked' no-start events.
records.solution: Verify the VIN against the ICCU recalls (Genesis 025G; NHTSA 24V-204 and its expansions). Dealers inspect and replace the ICCU and its fuse as necessary and apply updated ICCU software, free of charge. If you experience warning lights plus a power-reduction message, pull over and arrange transport rather than continuing to drive. A repeat dead-12V battery on an Electrified GV70 should trigger an ICCU diagnosis, not just a battery swap.
symptoms: Loss of drive power / reduced propulsion while driving
Audible 'pop' then warning lights and alarms
Repeated dead 12V battery / no-start ('bricked')
Vehicle fails to DC fast charge or AC charge
Check electric vehicle system warning

records.title: Infotainment Screen Freeze and Reboot
records.description: The GV70 infotainment system occasionally freezes mid-use, requiring the vehicle to be restarted to recover. The screen may go black or become unresponsive to touch and rotary controller inputs during navigation or media playback.
records.solution: Hold the power/volume knob for 10 seconds to force a soft reset. Update to the latest software via OTA or dealer visit. Clear the navigation cache and reduce stored Bluetooth device pairings.
symptoms: Screen freezing during use
System rebooting while driving
Touch and rotary inputs unresponsive
CarPlay disconnecting

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11002757 - Incomplete AVN OTA Update

records.title: Instrument Cluster Blank or Flickering at Startup
records.description: Incorrect software logic in the screen-initialization protocol (memory loading and error storage) can cause the digital instrument panel cluster to flicker or go completely blank at startup. When the cluster is inoperative, critical information such as the speedometer, fuel/charge gauge, and certain warning lights is obscured, which fails to comply with FMVSS 101 and increases crash risk. Genesis issued recall 031G covering the 2025 ICE GV70 and 2023-2025 Electrified GV70 (and GV80/G80), affecting roughly 32,500-36,000 vehicles. Owners report the cluster staying dark on start with a center screen that is unaffected.
records.solution: Check the VIN against Genesis recall 031G. The remedy is a free instrument-panel-display software update; on many vehicles it is delivered as an over-the-air (OTA) update, otherwise the dealer reflashes the cluster. If the cluster is blank, do not drive relying on the center screen; have the update applied.
symptoms: Instrument cluster blank or black at startup
Cluster flickering or partially inoperative
Missing speedometer / gauges
Warning lights not displaying
Cluster recovers after restart but recurs

records.title: Low-Pressure Fuel Pump Impeller Failure Causing Stalling
records.description: The low-pressure fuel pump assembly can contain an impeller made from material that does not meet specification. Under high ambient temperatures the impeller deforms and interferes with the pump housing, creating mechanical resistance that shuts the pump down and starves the engine of fuel. The result is a sudden loss of motive power or an engine stall while driving, which can happen at speed and create a crash risk. Genesis addressed it under safety recalls 016G and 022G (NHTSA 23V-630 and 24V-282), covering 2022-2023 GV70 along with G80/GV80/G90.
records.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recalls 23V-630 / 24V-282 (Genesis 016G/022G). The free remedy is replacement of the low-pressure fuel pump assembly using the recall service kit and tool per Genesis TSB 23-01-083G. Owners noticing stalling, hesitation, or hard starts in hot weather should have the recall completed before further driving.
symptoms: Sudden engine stall while driving
Loss of motive power
Hard starting or no-start, especially in hot weather
Engine hesitation or stumbling
Check engine light

records.title: Paint Color Mismatch Between Plastic Trim and Metal Body Panels (Uyuni White)
records.description: GV70 owners, most prominently on Uyuni White, report that painted plastic components (lower bumper mouldings, wheel-well trim, and fuel-filler door) are visibly one to two shades lighter than the adjacent metal body panels, sometimes from the factory at very low mileage; some describe an almost bluish hue on the mouldings. GV70e/Electrified owners report the same mismatch on wheel-well mouldings. Dealers frequently attribute it to plastic and metal accepting paint differently, and warranty repaint claims are often denied on that basis. This is an exterior/body finish issue.
records.solution: When Genesis accepts the claim, the dealer body shop repaints or color-blends the mismatched panel to body color under the paint/finish warranty (some owners have had rear bumpers replaced). Many owners are told the difference is 'inherent' to the metal/plastic materials and are denied, in which case an independent body-shop repaint of the affected bumper or trim panel is the out-of-pocket remedy.
symptoms: Front/rear bumper a lighter shade than the body panels
Lower plastic mouldings noticeably off-color (bluish hue)
Fuel-filler door does not match surrounding paint
Wheel-well trim mismatched on GV70e models
Mismatch visible even at very low mileage

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10235566 - Paint Protection Film Clouding

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof / Headliner Rattle and Wind Noise
records.description: GV70 owners report a rattle, click, or buzzing noise from the panoramic sunroof / headliner area, typically near the rear-view mirror, that appears when the body flexes over bumps or uneven pavement. Some also hear a gurgling sound at the sunroof edges above ~50 mph after heavy rain (trapped water moving in the roof). The noise is a common refinement complaint on an otherwise premium-feeling cabin. Genesis addressed it with TSB 23-BD-014G, which adds a felt kit and modified sunroof-frame bolts to eliminate movement.
records.solution: Have the dealer apply TSB 23-BD-014G: install the felt anti-rattle kit and the modified sunroof-frame bolts, and add foam/rubber padding behind the headliner where it contacts the sunroof frame. The repair typically requires removing the headliner and sunroof assembly and is covered under the new-vehicle warranty.
symptoms: Rattle or click from the sunroof/headliner near the rear-view mirror
Buzzing over bumps and uneven roads
Wind or gurgling noise at the sunroof edges at speed
Creaking from the front of the headliner

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 10251292 - GV70 Panoramic Sunroof Wind Noise

records.title: Rear Differential / eLSD Whine and Repeat Carrier Failure
records.description: AWD GV70s (both 2.5T and 3.5T) develop a whining, humming, or droning noise from the rear axle, often at highway speed and frequently before the break-in period is even over. The condition is tied to the rear differential carrier and, on Sport/3.5T trims, the electronic limited-slip differential (eLSD). Genesis acknowledged it with TSB 23-DS-004G / 23-DS-004G-1, which walks dealers through noise inspection, lock-nut re-torque, re-inspection, and full carrier replacement. The biggest owner frustration is repeat failure: dealers swap in the same-design carrier and the replacement units whine again within thousands of miles, with one 3.5T owner reporting a second failure at ~3,700 miles after a new carrier and another reporting two eLSD replacements under 8,000 miles.
records.solution: Have the dealer perform TSB 23-DS-004G/-1: inspect and re-torque the differential carrier lock nut, road-test, and if noise persists replace the rear differential carrier assembly (and the eLSD-equipped carrier on Sport/3.5T) under the 5yr/60k powertrain warranty, followed by a rear-axle alignment. Because the same-design part can fail again, document each occurrence in writing for lemon-law leverage and ask whether an updated revision carrier is available before authorizing a like-for-like swap.
symptoms: Whining or humming from the rear of the vehicle
Droning noise that rises with road speed
Noise present from very low mileage
Recurrence of noise shortly after a differential replacement
Occasional rear-axle vibration

records.title: Sunroof Drain Clog Causing Water Leak Into Cabin
records.description: GV70s with the panoramic sunroof can leak water into the cabin during heavy rain because the sunroof drainage tubes clog or the original drain plug design lets water back up. Owners report damp headliner, water on the seats or floor, and in some cases a sloshing sound in the roof. Genesis released a TSB with a revised drain-plug design, and dealers have cleared/replaced drains under warranty.
records.solution: Have the dealer clear the front and rear sunroof drain tubes and install the revised drain-plug design per the applicable TSB. If interior trim or the headliner is wet, ask the dealer to inspect for mold and dry/replace affected material. Owners in heavy-rain regions can periodically check that the drain channels are clear.
symptoms: Water dripping into the cabin during heavy rain
Damp headliner, seats, or floor
Sloshing/gurgling water sound in the roof
Musty odor from interior
Wet A-pillar or footwell

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11027794 - GV70 Sunroof Drain Plugs

records.title: Transmission Harness Water Leak Causing Park-to-Neutral Rollaway
records.description: Blanking pins were incorrectly installed in the transmission control harness connectors at the supplier, allowing water to enter the connectors and cause an electrical short. The short can make the transmission controls erroneously and unexpectedly shift from Park to Neutral, allowing the vehicle to roll away if the parking brake is not set. Genesis recall 020G (NHTSA 24V-205) covers roughly 15,645 GV70 built May 10, 2023 to Feb 25, 2024.
records.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recall 24V-205 (Genesis 020G). Dealers inspect the transmission control harness and repair the connector or replace the harness and internal wiring as necessary, free of charge. Until repaired, always set the emergency/parking brake and turn the ignition off when parked.
symptoms: Vehicle unexpectedly shifts from Park to Neutral
Vehicle rolls when parked without the parking brake set
Transmission warning messages
Intermittent shift-by-wire faults after rain or car washes

records.title: 2.5L T-GDI Cold-Start Misfire P0300-P0304 (Service Campaign 914G / TSB 25-01-051G)
records.description: Theta III 2.5L T-GDI engines in GV80 JX1 (and related G80/GV70) illuminate the Check Engine light with random or specific cylinder misfire codes P0300-P0304 during cold start. Root cause is identified as ECM misfire-detection logic; Genesis issued service campaign 914G covering 2021-2024MY GV80 built 07/27/2020-03/04/2024 for a free ECM reflash.
records.solution: Free dealer remedy under Service Campaign 914G / TSB 25-01-051G: ~30 minute ECM software reflash with improved misfire logic. Persistent misfire after reflash warrants coil/injector swap-test on the affected cylinder.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on after cold start
Rough idle during warm-up
Brief stumble or shudder on first start of the day
Multi-cylinder or cylinder-specific misfire codes

records.title: Harsh ride and impact harshness on 22-inch wheels (E-Supercharger trim)
records.description: The GV80 Coupe's 22-inch wheels — standard on the 3.5T E-Supercharger AWD trim (the base 3.5T AWD uses 20-inch wheels) — produce a choppy, busy ride over expansion joints, tar strips, and broken pavement. Per The Drive review, the choppiness is 'undoubtedly exacerbated by its massive 22-inch wheels.' Owners report vehicles delivered at 40-44 psi cold (transport pressure); dropping to door-placard 33-35 psi noticeably softens ride. The 22-inch tire sidewall is ~4.2 inches versus ~5.2 inches on the 20-inch package, eliminating roughly an inch of sidewall absorption.
records.solution: First, verify cold tire pressure matches door placard (typically 33-35 psi); many vehicles arrive over-inflated for transport. If still harsh, consider swapping to the 20-inch wheel/tire package (better sidewall absorption) or higher-sidewall winter set.
symptoms: jarring over potholes and expansion joints
tire/wheel noise on coarse pavement
steering wheel tremor on broken pavement

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11006122 - GV80 Coupe Battery Drain

records.title: Diesel NOx System Issues (International Markets)
records.description: Diesel GV80 models experience NOx aftertreatment system issues, including SCR catalyst efficiency codes and DEF quality warnings. The NOx sensor can give false readings, triggering regeneration cycles and reduced power modes.
records.solution: Replace the NOx sensor and clear adaptation values. Use only manufacturer-approved DEF fluid. Update the ECU calibration for improved NOx system management. Avoid short trips that prevent the DPF from completing regeneration.
symptoms: DEF quality warning message
Reduced engine power mode
Frequent DPF regeneration cycles
Check engine light with NOx codes

records.title: Front Seat Belt Pretensioner Can Explode and Project Metal Fragments (Recall NHTSA 23V094)
records.description: Driver and front-passenger seat belt pretensioners can build excessive internal pressure and rupture upon deployment in a crash, projecting metal fragments into the cabin and injuring occupants. Genesis recalled ~65,500 vehicles across multiple models (GV80, G80, GV70, GV60), with GV80 units built July 2020 through December 2022 affected.
records.solution: Free recall remedy: dealer installs a protective metal cap over the front pretensioners to contain any rupture. Verify VIN at NHTSA.gov under campaign 23V094; call Genesis at 855-371-9460 to schedule.
symptoms: Pretensioner ruptures during crash deployment
Metal fragments expelled into cabin
Risk of serious injury during airbag/belt deployment

records.title: Head-Up Display Fades / 'Eclipse' Effect Before Total Failure
records.description: GV80 owners describe the HUD progressively fading from one side (an 'eclipse' moving across the projection) until 80-90% of the display is blocked, then briefly recovering. Many units intermittently fail for months before going completely dark and requiring full HUD assembly replacement. Cause is typically LCD/projector overheating or hardware failure, not the windshield.
records.solution: Rule out polarized sunglasses (which kill HUD visibility) and direct sun overheating of the projector. If fade persists when cool, request HUD projector module replacement under 5yr/60k bumper-to-bumper warranty; out of warranty, full unit replacement runs ~$1100-$2200 installed.
symptoms: HUD dims or fades from one side
Round dark area sweeps across HUD image
HUD intermittently disappears then returns
Eventually HUD stops projecting entirely

records.title: Infotainment and Connected Services Issues
records.description: The GV80 infotainment system experiences periodic software glitches, including the 3D navigation display freezing, wireless phone charging overheating phones, and Genesis Connected Services failing to communicate with the vehicle.
records.solution: Update to the latest infotainment and Connected Services software. Disable wireless charging if phone overheating occurs and use a wired connection. Factory reset the head unit for persistent glitches.
symptoms: 3D navigation display freezing
Phone overheating on wireless charger
Connected Services app not connecting
Split screen mode glitching

records.title: Instrument Cluster Goes Blank at Startup - Software Logic Error (Recall NHTSA 25V105)
records.description: An erroneous logic condition in the instrument cluster controller software can leave the digital cluster display inoperative or intermittent at startup, hiding the speedometer, fuel gauge, and warning lamps. NHTSA recall 25V105 (Genesis internal 026G) covers approximately 32,594 Genesis vehicles total across GV80, GV70, and G80 — including 2023-2024 GV80 units produced January 6, 2023 through March 6, 2024. Owner notifications were mailed March 26, 2025.
records.solution: Free recall remedy: Genesis dealer performs a software update to the cluster controller; no hardware replacement required. Confirm coverage via VIN lookup at NHTSA.gov under campaign 25V105.
symptoms: Digital gauge cluster blank at startup
Speedometer and tachometer not visible
Warning lights not displayed
Display flickers or comes on intermittently

records.title: Low-Pressure Fuel Pump Impeller Deformation Causes Stalling (Recall 022G / NHTSA 24V282)
records.description: The low-pressure fuel pump impeller can deform under high ambient temperatures, causing it to interfere with the pump housing and shut down. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation/stumbling, MIL illumination, and engine stall while driving. Genesis recalled ~31,440 GV70/GV80/G80/G90 vehicles; GV80 production dates Nov 4 2021 through Sep 13 2022.
records.solution: Free recall remedy: Genesis dealer will replace the low-pressure fuel pump assembly. Owners should call Genesis at 855-371-9460 or check VIN at NHTSA.gov to confirm coverage under campaign 24V282 / Recall 022G.
symptoms: Engine stalls while driving
Hesitation or stumbling under load
Rough idle
Check Engine Light
No-start after heat soak

records.title: Rear Differential Hum/Whine Noise from Improperly Torqued Pinion Lock Nut (TSB 23-DS-004G)
records.description: Owners report a humming, whining or howling noise from the rear differential that changes with vehicle speed and is most noticeable during steady cruise between approximately 35-75 mph. Genesis TSB 23-DS-004G (Aug 2023) and revision 23-DS-004G-1 identify an improperly torqued pinion lock nut from the factory causing incorrect ring-and-pinion mesh. Dealer first installs a repair kit (bolts + nut) and re-torques per spec; full rear differential assembly replacement is required if noise persists. The same TSB also covers 2021-2024 G80 (RG3) and 2022-2024 GV70 (JK1/JK1A) — chassis code for GV80 is JX1.
records.solution: Have dealer perform TSB 23-DS-004G inspection: install repair kit (2 bolts + 1 nut) and re-torque pinion lock nut first; replace rear differential assembly if noise persists. Repair is covered under Genesis 10yr/100k powertrain warranty - document the noise on a repair order before warranty expires.
symptoms: Whine or howl from rear of vehicle on acceleration
Hum that changes pitch with road speed
Noise unchanged when turning (distinguishes from wheel bearing)
Drone between 30-60 mph

citations.title: Genesis Bulletin 11009768 - GV80 Rear Differential Noise
